mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, increasing the present value of future earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months while S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0% for two consecutive months and S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST > 650,000 units) and retail sales (RSAFS > $400 billion) indicates robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: HOUST > 650 and RSAFS > 400 billion in the same month but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: Low industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) indicates supply-side constraints that limit corporate output capacity and profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 for two consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 130,000 thousand persons) strengthens consumer spending power and corporate revenue streams, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate demand expansion.
failure_condition: PAYEMS > 130,000 for three consecutive months and S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) triggers expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes that increase borrowing costs and reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% for two consecutive months and S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) and restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS >= 0.10%) suppress consumer spending and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through dual economic headwinds.
regime_hint: weak labor market with restrictive policy
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0% and FEDFUNDS >= 0.10% in the same month but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for three consecutive months) increases risk-free rates and reduces liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through higher discount rates on equity cash flows.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for three consecutive months and S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods.
